Vertical Scales or Vertically Moderated
 Standards Setting
• Construction of a developmental scale:
 – The Holy Grail of scale construction? See Briggs and Rekase.
• Scale requirements for student growth?
 – Do we need VSS/VMSS to discuss student growth?
• Questions:
 – VSS/VMSS are designed to answer very different questions about student growth
 and the two are mutually exclusive. (Later in the same paragraph: “If it is not
 possible for a state to implement vertical scaling measures, VMSS may be used
 to track student growth across years”)
 – If a state has a VSS, can’t they add VMSS on top?
 – Lissitz and Huynh argued that if a state is considering implements a system that
 focuses on progression within achievement levels and desires a system that will
 provide meaningful information on classroom instruction and teacher adaptation,
 then vertical scales would not be appropriate.
 – “The most useful method for measuring student growth across all grades would
 be vertically equated scores, scaled to yield equal interval scores” (Clemens
 1993)
